author: The Church of England (Book of Common Prayer)
work: The Order for the Burial of the Dead
section: The Committal (said as earth is cast upon the body)
translation: Book of Common Prayer (1662), public domain
note: The classic Western Christian burial committal, from the 1662 BCP. The 'earth to earth, ashes to ashes, dust to dust' wording is the culturally familiar form of the Christian hope of resurrection at a graveside; the closing clause alludes to Philippians 3:21. Bound as an Anglican-tradition liturgical text, not the only or normative rite — the resurrection hope it voices is common ground across traditions, but the specific wording is the 1662 BCP's. NOT a modern (copyrighted) revision such as Common Worship or the 1979 US BCP; only the genuinely public-domain 1662 text. The full-book official PD scan is justus.anglican.org/resources/bcp/1662/Baskerville.pdf; the section-specific source_url above shows this committal verbatim. Verified 2026-08-17 (apologia-citations, web): text, capitalization ('Resurrection' capitalized; divine pronouns lower-case) and punctuation confirmed exact against the official 1662 BCP; diagnostic words 'take' (not the Canadian revision's 'receive') and 'vile' (not 'mortal') confirm the older 1662 form; nothing modernized; Philippians 3:21 (KJV/Coverdale) allusion confirmed. 1662 BCP is public domain in the US and treated as PD internationally.
text: Forasmuch as it hath pleased Almighty God of his great mercy to take unto himself the soul of our dear brother here departed, we therefore commit his body to the ground; earth to earth, ashes to ashes, dust to dust; in sure and certain hope of the Resurrection to eternal life, through our Lord Jesus Christ; who shall change our vile body, that it may be like unto his glorious body, according to the mighty working, whereby he is able to subdue all things to himself.
